name: CodeAtlas
platform: macOS and Windows; local browser mode
summary: Explore source code through repository indexing, explanations and architecture maps.
intro: CodeAtlas combines a local code index with an embedded editor and optional AI explanations. Trace symbols, inspect evidence and build repository documentation from the selected workspace.

features.title: Repository index
features.body: Scan source code and track changes with symbol and relationship indexing.

features.title: Explain and navigate
features.body: Inspect symbol explanations, callers, callees and supporting evidence.

features.title: Maps and documentation
features.body: Create query-driven code maps and repository documentation.

features.title: Workspace editor
features.body: Read and edit files with document overlays and save controls.

support.title: Choose a workspace
paragraphs: Open Settings, select the repository folder and apply it. Follow the restart prompt when changing the active workspace.

support.title: Configure explanations
paragraphs: Set an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model in Settings. Generated explanations require a working provider; check connection errors and credentials if configuration is incomplete.

support.title: Semantic tools
paragraphs: Optional language servers improve semantic evidence. Missing servers reduce precision but do not replace the local parser index.

support.title: Review generated output
paragraphs: Follow citations to source and check inferred behavior before relying on explanations or proposed changes.

privacy.title: Local repository data
paragraphs: CodeAtlas reads the selected workspace and stores a derived SQLite index, normally in a .codeatlas directory within that workspace. Saved editor changes modify the selected source files.

privacy.title: AI requests
paragraphs: Generated explanations and documentation send prompts and relevant source evidence to the configured chat endpoint. A remote provider receives that content; provider connection tests also make requests.

privacy.title: Settings and credentials
paragraphs: Settings are stored for the current operating-system user. Credentials entered through Settings use the system credential vault; credentials supplied through environment files remain governed by how those files are stored.

privacy.title: Local interface
paragraphs: The default server listens on the loopback interface and the desktop app uses an embedded web view. Changing the listen address changes who may be able to reach the service.

privacy.title: Removal and diagnostics
paragraphs: Quit the app before removing a derived index or local settings. Remove saved credentials through the configured credential controls and manage source files and exports separately. No integrated analytics or crash-reporting service was found in the inspected source.
